corrected_value.title_o: Clinical Utility of the 3-ounce Water Swallow Test

decisions.quote:
Multiple, double-blinded raters and
VFSS as the reference standard confirmed previous
research that used a single, nonblinded rater and FEES as
the reference standard [2].
decisions.location: Conclusion, lines 272-275 (and Discussion, lines 188-189; Reference 2, lines 347-348)
decisions.reason: Both the shipped row and blind target 0 identify the same replicated original study: Reference [2], Suiter & Leder (published online 2007, in print 2008, 'Clinical utility of the 3 ounce water swallow test', Dysphagia 2008;23:244-50, DOI 10.1007/s00455-007-9127-y). The paper explicitly states that this systematic replication study verified and confirmed the findings of [2].

decisions.quote:
The clinical validity, reliability, and usefulness of the Yale
Swallow Protocol for determining aspiration risk were
confirmed. All participants who were deemed not to be an
aspiration risk based on results of the protocol also did not
aspirate during VFSS. Multiple, double-blinded raters and
VFSS as the reference standard confirmed previous
research that used a single, nonblinded rater and FEES as
the reference standard [2].
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding agree on 'successful'. The authors explicitly conclude that their systematic replication study verified and confirmed the previous research findings [2], achieving 100% sensitivity and 100% negative predictive value for identifying aspiration risk.

decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding agree on 'replication'. This prospective, double-blinded, multirater systematic replication study collected new swallowing assessment data from 25 consecutive adult male patients using multiple blinded raters and videofluoroscopy (VFSS) to re-test the previously published 3-ounce water swallow / Yale Swallow Protocol aspiration-risk findings of Suiter & Leder [2].
